There is a strange evil in the air.

I can feel my mind slipping. Is this island cursed? While I write these words, I can feel myself teetering on the precipice of madness. Some of the crew, their minds have passed the point of no return. 

We embarked on an expedition into the mountains today. Whispers of a mutiny seep through the ship, and their accusing eyes tell me I'm their scapegoat. First Mate Rolf whispered of a plot, with Barnacle Bess at its helm, a treacherous scheme to usurp my authority.

I must act, lest they act first.
Captain's Log (1/4)

The treasure we took from the Sankari islands. It haunts me. It consumes my thoughts, my every waking moment.

I've hidden it away, buried within the depths of this forsaken mountain. It's safely concealed now. No one except myself knows where it is. I have drawn a map to the treasure's location. It is my treasure, and none shall have it.

Trust is a luxury I can no longer afford.
Captain's Log (2/4)

I believe I can still trust my first mate. Rolf is different than the mutineers. He seems unswayed by these whispers that taunt me from the shadows. His mind seems less touched by the madness that I know has taken hold of me. I can use him to guide me through this darkness

I don't think about the Sankari treasure any longer. I saw unreachable vaults of gold buried deep behind an unmovable gate. We've been calling them the Golden Vaults—an enigma shrouded in a veil of legends. 

But for now, we abandoned them. There are urgent matters to attend to. Once I rid myself of Barnacle Bess' traitorous scoundrels, I shall venture forth with the rest of my loyal crew.
Captain's Log (3/4)

I have entrusted Rolf with the map to the Sankari treasure. A perilous burden for a loyal friend. He's oblivious of the expedition's true cost—the lives of those who once called me Captain. My hands are tainted with their blood, a grim deed in the name of safeguarding my treasure.

I slashed their throats in their sleep. One by one. Out of my own depravity. My own insanity.

Gods... what have I become?
Captain's Log (4/4)
Pirates from the same crew are killing one another. The curse of this island has rendered all of them insane.

This Demo serves as a representation of our pre-alpha development phase, and is specifically organized to replicate the final experience inside a small gameplay loop, with up to 2 hours of gameplay.

Our primary focus is to give an immersive gameplay experience for the players. This is demonstrated through the game's core loop which feratures a fast-paced souls-lite combat, and metroidvania-like exploration and progression.

It is important to note that the development of the game is still ongoing and, as such, additional content will be added along with polished version of the existing content.

We hope that you find the Pre-Alpha Demo enjoyable and we welcome feedback that you may have refarding the game.
Mark of the Deep

Mark of the Deep is a story-rich action adventure game where the player controls Markus “Rookie” Ramsey, a rookie pirate, exploring the mysteries of a cursed island in order to find the lost pirate crew, lift the island’s curse and leave.

A pirate ship wrecked in a mystic and cursed island, till then known only by myths n’ tales. Rookie face all perils to find his lost crew. However, by exploring the eerie biomes and 
fighting abyssal monsters, he will learn that the Island was cursed centuries ago, when the cultist leader of the Old Folks, the native inhabitants of the island, imprisoned the Leviathan in the pursuit of Immortality.

Mark of the Deep is inspired by both Hollow Knight and Death's Door as it has strong elements of metroidvanias, with a rich world and is an isometric action adventure game filled with different abilities and mechanics.
Story Summary

The Story of the Angry Mermaid Pirates starts with the story of their Captain, James Ramsey. James began his life at sea as a sailor for the Imperial Navy, following a famous privateer named Monty Pollock. 
Pollock was betrayed by the Imperials, and together with his crew they decided to become independent plunderers.

James was Pollock’s most trusted advisor, and they sank enough ships and amassed enough gold to become feared and famous throughout the seven seas. 
Even Imperial ships would try to flee when they saw the infamous black flag of the Rising Storm.

Twenty years ago, when the Rising Storm was docked, Pollock was captured and hung by the Imperials. Most of the original crew disbanded and went into hiding. 
James Ramsey fled to an ocean side town, where he met Rookie’s mother. They fell in love. But during a night of storms, he realized his life belonged to the seas. He was planning to leave. 
She told him she was pregnant. He left without saying a word.

Eventually, Ramsey found some of his old shipmates, including Eduardo Ortega. He confessed to Ortega that he had impregnated one of the locals, but he 
wasn't a role model, and therefore convinced himself that the boy would be better off without him. 

Together with his old crewmates, skilled pirates as they were, they managed to steal a ship from the Imperial Fleet in a night of outstanding glory.

They swapped the imperial flag for skull and crossbones, and the ship became known as the Angry Mermaid. The new crewmembers were unanimous in giving Ramsey the title of Captain, the oldest and wisest of them all.  
Ortega became his First Mate. Word quickly spread that the successors of the legendary pirate Monty Pollock were back.

But with the tenacity of someone who devoted his entire life to being at sea and a crew that was considered the best and most loyal among all pirates, Captain James Ramsey became even more famous than Pollock. 
They were feared and admired, and Ramsey had everything he could ever dream of.

Time passed, and his mind started failing him. He was the bravest and the strongest, but he felt his wit escaping. His mind became elusive. 
He started faltering in front of his crew, who all reminded him that it’s what happened with age, and it was normal. That he had the best pirates in the world, and they would follow him to the end of the ocean, if he so desired. 

Ramsey was never afraid of death, but he was afraid of madness. And if that’s what his old age would bring him, he had to do something about it. 
One day, during one of the crew's expeditions, they had to stop in an distant island to resupply their ship. In this island, Ramsey, Ortega and Screech found an old woman. During a whole night she told them several ancient stories. 
One of them being about a specific ritual. And thus, Captain James Ramsey took possession of the knowledge on how to perform the Blood Ritual.

Ortega and Screech didn't take any of these stories seriously, thinking it was just an old and senile woman. However, for the Captain it was differently. 
The idea of becoming immortal and beating the natural order of life, not becoming mad and losing his mind, started to corrupt his heart. From this point on, he only could think about how he could perform the Blood Ritual.

The main issue, though, was that he knew that if he told the crew about it they would definitely think he was mad and the Angry Mermaid Pirates would depose him. So he kept it to himself.

As time passed, he started to ask Screech for old tales and myths. He studied the stories about an old and different people that used to wage war against the mainlanders. 
He went after children songs about an island that vanished thousand's of years ago. Also, he started to believe the tales that when a lot of people die in the sea at the same time no body is left behind.

No one will never know if the Captain knew what he was doing or was pure sheer of luck due to his growing madness, but he realized that  on his own on how to use the Blood Ritual. 
He knew that he would need to make a huge sacrifice, he would need to have his crew killed in order to find the vanishing island and thus use the Blood Ritual to gain immortality.

During the following months, the Captain became more ominous and silent. The crew thought he was having trouble dealing with his condition and thought it was best to leave him alone. 
He gave orders to the crew to go to sail during the hurricane season. Everyone thought it was odd, it didn't make sense to sail during these periods. But nonetheless, they crew followed his orders at their best. Only Ortega was weary. 
He knew the Captain for too long to know that something was going on. But he need to keep it for himself before accuse the Captain of anything.

And then, the Angry Mermaid Pirates sailed for the last time.

One day, suddenly, the open sky was taken by the darkest of storms. The sailors were having trouble keeping the ship in one piece. For the first time in their lives, most of them did not think they would survive the storm.  
Screech saw strange lights coming from the Captain's cabin and started to hear weird sounds from it.

Screech associated the chant the Captain was making with the words of the old woman. He quickly understood that the Captain could be trying to sacrifice the whole crew. 
He ran to Ortega to let him know what was about to happen. The First Mate, then, busted the cabin’s door open. The Captain was engulfed in a torrent of ghostly light, a light that was flowing into him from the ocean. It was almost over, and Ortega could feel it.

As fast as he could, Ortega took his sword and pierced through the Captain’s heart. Yet, the ship started to sink, and the Angry Mermaid Pirates started to die. 
Suddenly, the survivors and the wrecks appeared falling into an island that wasn't supposed to be there. The rest is history.

Thousands of years ago, there was a people of ancient seafarers known as the Old Folks. They lived in an ancient Island that vanished long time ago. Nowadays, there's no sign of either the Island and the Old Folks.

The Old Folks lived in a theocratic society, where  the priests were their leaders, spiritually and politically. The deity they worshiped was known as the Leviathan, a deep sea-monster, responsible to take 
the soul of the dead from the world of the living to the underworld.

Early in their civilization, the Leviathan gave his blessing to the Island, giving it the Mark of the Deep. This helped the Old Folks civilization to thrive and grow. Throughout the Island, the Old Folks 
found rocks and waterfalls with the Mark of the Deep and, around those, they created Shrines and founded their first settlements around them.

For several centuries, the Old Folk civilization grew more and more under the blessing of the Mark of the Deep. They mastered civil engineering, being able to explore and occupy the majority of the Island. 
Inspired by the Hellenistic period, they founded their Capital at the center of the Island and built roads from all parts. All of them leading to the Capital.

With their growth, the Old Folks started to reach the outside world, getting in touch with several other civilization. This exchange gave them a lot of knowledge and they were able, through time, to create 
the Great Library, filled with ancient books and powerful artifacts.

However, their period of wars started as well. For several centuries the Old Folks battled and held their island. They were never expansionists. They always believed that the reason they thrived was 
because of the Marks of the Deep and they could only find it inside the Island.

At their peak, the Old Folks were led by Reverend Faidon Tolakus. He was really liked by his people and considered a good leader overall. However, the inherited the leadership in a period of a long lasting war. 
Through decades the war wasn't even near of ending, and this constant state of warfare started to impact the livelihood of the Old Folks.

One day, a young orphan who grew up with the gift of visions. His name was Takon Erodus. He quickly was adopted by the priests for his gift and was put under the guidance of Reverend Faidon. 
Takon soon joined the priesthood and gained the title of the Knower. He used his visions to predict the future and help the islanders to grow crops and protect them from storms.

As the war started to threaten the Old Folks civilization, Takon decided to leave the Island, in a pilgrimage to find the power to end the war. 
Faidon was categorically against Takon's plan, saying that it wasn't their way to find power for warfare, that they thrived by being diplomatic and traders. But Takon left anyway.

In this travels, Takon met and old woman. She was an outcast living alone in a hut. She told him several ancient stories. One of them being about a specific ritual. 
And thus, Takon took possession of the knowledge on how to perform the Blood Ritual, a barely know ritual that allows the user to trap and absorb the powers of a deity, granting mythical powers and immortality.

Takon struggled with this knowledge. At one hand he knew that no such power should be used as messing the gods were a risk. 
At the other hand he knew that with this power he would be able to not just end the war and save the Old Folks, but also allow their civilization to expand beyond Island.

The thoughts of his power started to corrupt his mind, making him more and more obsessed to gain power. However, the only deity he knew was the Leviathan and it was the patron of his civilization. 
He knew, then, that he needed to do at least two things in order to gain his new powers: he needed to bring the Leviathan inside the Island, so he could perform the Blood Ritual; also he needed the support of the Old Folks, so he could lead them as their new leader.

When Takon returned, they started a dissident religion within the Old Folks, the Cult of the Deep. As Faidon's leadership was weakening due to the war and the news of Takon's return started to reach all side of the Island, the Cult of the Deep grew like wildfire. 
Soon, a civil war started. One side led by Faidon and the other, by Takon. 

The Cult of the Deep started to increase the mining activity at the Island, defiling several Shrines, using their stones to create masks for their followers, each of these masks bearing the Mark of the Deep.

It didn't take long for Takon to conquer the Capital and dethrone Faidon. At this point, the step one of his plans was done. He became the leader of the Old Folks. However, he still needed to imprison the Leviathan. 
Takon, then, gathered the Old Folks in one of the Island's beaches, claiming that he would make a parade for his new coronation and grant a pardon for the ones that fought alongside Faidon. 
Actually, what he was gambling was to create such a massacre, by killing everyone that didn't join the Cult of the Deep. His idea was that by killing so many people near the beach Leviathan would appear, even though they were in land. 

And he was correct. When Takon ordered the Cultists of the Deep to attack the other Old Folks and the massacre started, it didn't take long for the Leviathan to appear to collect their souls. 
At this moment, Takon used the Blood Ritual and imprisoned the Leviathan inside the island and stole his powers.

However, what Takon didn't foresee was that the Leviathan isn't a creature of the world of the living. Because of this, even though the Leviathan is imprisoned in the Island, he went back 
to his plane of existence, bringing the Island with him. From this point on, the Island left the world of the living, entrapping all the Old Folks inside it.

The other side effect of having the Leviathan trapped inside the Island was that the Abyssal Corruption started. The Old Folks started to transform into fish-like men, the fauna and the flora as well, started to be affected by it. 
Only those near the Shrines bearing the Mark of the Deep were spared of the Abyssal Corruption. 

The Cultists of the Deep were safe of the corruption because all their masks bare the Mark of the Deep, taken from desecrated shrines. 
The survivors of the Old Folks, however, didn't share the same fate. Takon's new objective was to find a way to free the Leviathan and save the Island but keeping his powers. His ambitions were way beyond the Island. 
He knew that with such power he could conquer the rest of the world.

Faidon, at the other hand, were able to survive the Blood Ritual and fled with the remaining of this followers. They hid in the forest and started the Opposition, a group which solely purpose was to defeat Takon. 
However, he knew that they couldn't defeat the Cult of the Deep by brute force, for either they were outnumbered but they were becoming monsters due to the Abyssal Corruption.

Even though they couldn't defeat Takon, the opposition knew that they could at least stop them from leaving the Island and conquering the world. But this option would mean them also staying inside the island forever.

Inside the Great Library there was a powerful artifact, the Soul Jar. With this item Faidon captured Takon's essence, as well from the Cultists of the Deep, leaving them transformed into unbreakable stones. 
The ritual that Faidon performed was a forbidden sacrament known as the Stone Enchantment.

The Opposition was able to stop the Cult of the Deep. However, they still needed to protect the Soul Jar. Breaking the Soul Jar means reverting the Stone Enchantment. 
Because of the Abyssal Corruption, the Opposition knew that it would be just a matter of time until someone would try to break the Soul Jar.

To protect it, the Opposition hid the Soul Jar at the top of the Island's dormant volcano and locked the only passage to it. They divided the key in 3 parts and also hid them through the Island. 
One at the Old Folk vaults, at the top of the High Peaks. One inside the Great Library and one at the Lighthouse. Only by destroying these 3 keys the volcano door will open. They made an oath to never talk about this and went into hiding as villagers. 
They were able to protect their minds through the ages and never talked about what happened with anyone. As long as they kept their minds in shape, they would live almost forever, slowly being consumed by the corruption.

The Old Folks were gone from the world. Doomed to live as monsters inside an isolated island in another plane of existence.

The coast of the island used to be a place for the Old Folk to dock their ships when coming back from expeditions in other lands. As a consequence of the civil war and Takon's blood ritual, the coast fell into devastation. Cultists ravaged the surrounding structures, staining the sea with the blood of innocents and leaving the area in ruins.

The Abyssal Woods stand as a chilling testament to the corruption's indiscriminate reach, even affecting plant life. Within its depths, once harmless flora turns bloodthirsty under the influence of corruption, posing a deadly threat to unwary travelers.

The ancient crossroads used to be a bustling hub of trade and community for the island's inhabitants. After the ravages of the civil war brought death and destruction to its once-thriving surroundings, it fell silent. The once-vibrant marketplace became desolate, now abandoned by the Old Folk who used to gather there. It is now an empty space, visited only by roaming animals and other beasts.

The capital of the island, once a beacon of prosperity and culture inhabited by Leviathan worshipers, now bears the scars of conflict. Amidst its grand buildings and reminders of conflict, any wanderer can tell the land has gone through hardships. Takon, leader of the Cult of the Deep, has claimed a throne that was once Faidon's, as a symbol of power over the island.

The Cathedral of the Deep, once filled with serenity and adorned with mesmerizing stained glass windows, lies in ruins following the civil war. Once a peaceful and cherished sanctuary for Old Folk devotion to Leviathan, it is now infested with lurking beasts hungry for blood, making it dangerous for anyone who ventures inside.

The Old Folk civilization relied on multiple economic pillars, including fishing, due to the rich sealife in the island bay. Fishermen established the Fishing Village near the shore for easier access to resources, with cooks and merchants also settling nearby for fresh fish. Today, remnants of these houses stand as silent reminders of the bustling community that once thrived there.

Once bustling with grand structures and corridors, these ruins served as pathways for the Old Folk to access the sealife-rich shore and other amenities of the island. In the aftermath of the civil war, however, destruction reigns, with the remains of these structures now submerged underwater from the shore.

The Forgotten Passageway, once a route to the High Peaks, became heavily guarded during the civil war to deter cultists. Presently, few successfully traverse it, as a vigilant mark keeper remains, ensuring its protection from intruders.

The Haven of the Free People, untouched by Abyssal Corruption, shelters the master shrine, believed to be the source of nourishment for all other shrines across the land. Yet, amid blessings and mysteries, one can never be too certain about the true workings of this arcane sanctuary.

The High Peaks, the island's tallest and chilliest spot, once demanded cautious passage from the Old Folk to avoid freezing. Today, the cold is compounded by the threat of roaming beasts, requiring even greater vigilance from travelers.

The Leviathan Temple, built by the Old Folk, once served as a sanctuary for their devotion to Leviathan. After the Stone Enchantment and the rise of the Mark Keepers, statues of these heroes, added by the Opposition, honor their powers, believed to stem from Leviathan's blessing. This integration of new guardians within the temple symbolizes the continuity of faith and protection against those who brought chaos to the island.

The Mausoleum stands as a timeless tribute to the departed. It was a place where the Old Folk could peacefully mourn those who have passed. As a sanctuary of remembrance in a land blessed by Leviathan, the Mausoleum stands as a testament to the enduring bond between the living and the dead.

During the era of peace among the Old Folk, treasure hunting was a common practice. With the onset of the civil war, the Opposition had to secure their relics. Fearing the Cult of the Deep's plundering, they sought a secure vault to safeguard their possessions effectively.

This curse shall be the death of me. When it was just scales and barnacles, I was fine, but now I look like a full-fledged fish-beast.

My mind is failing, and I have begun to experience hallucinations. I swear I've seen crabs trying to pinch me.

I always try to take walks to feel better, but somehow, I always end up at the same darned place: the Sacrificial Beach. The Ancient Crossroads were supposed to be more peaceful than the rest of this cursed island. Yet, whenever I venture too far south, I am reminded of that awful massacre...

Although I work hard to maintain my sanity, I often wonder what the point is. Clearly, insanity has overtaken me, and I will never be myself again.

Oh, Faidon. Is fighting the corruption better than yielding to it? This endless struggle... is it worth it?

During one of my walks across this land, I encountered a very interesting character. It had been a while since I last met those small people; still, most of them flee and scream right before becoming beasts themselves.

This man was different, though. He was interested in learning more about our people and our history. A fighter and a warrior, who even made friends with other Old Folk. He mentioned some names I hadn't heard in a while. He said he met some guy named Yonis... but also Faidon and Calanthus. It's great to know that there are some Mark Keepers who are still around.

He was heading toward some dark parts of the western ruins, though—places most people can't even reach. Still, he marched right into that area.

However, I couldn't shake my concern as he ventured toward the darker corners of the western ruins. Rumors abound of a king crab lurking in that area, and I fear for his safety. I hope those rumors remain just that, as facing such a beast would be a formidable challenge for any warrior.

I just hope nothing bad happens to him...

To anyone who reads this, I leave these words behind to my beloved ones.

As the drums of war grow louder, I must heed their call to safety. Know that my departure is not one of abandonment, but of necessity... and fear.

I shall flee to a cave not so far away, over the waterfalls and across the forgotten passageway. Who knows what the future holds? For me, hopefully not death.

Refuges sound lonely. Maybe someone will read this and come by, if I actually end up staying there for good.

That would be... cool.

I couldn't really trust my captain when she said there was a refuge in such an odd place. Yet, after my crew and I rampaged across those rocks and valleys to reach that haven, I was only glad to be alive and well.

Still, those waterfalls were driving me crazy. I couldn't spend one more minute there, regardless of how safe my crew and I were. I had to find a way to go home.

As I write this, scales are popping up on my skin, and breathing has become quite tough. I often wonder whether I should go back to that old passageway and cross that waterfall once again... But I don't think the Houfeng would ever accept someone who left them behind like that.

I'm afraid my end is near. I shall leave this letter behind for whoever needs protection from this curse to find.

Presently, former members of the Opposition linger, haunted by the impending threat of succumbing to Abyssal corruption.

Beyond its walls lies the gateway to the Abyssal Woods, a realm reserved for those who prove their worth in trial. When the Civil War struck, the stronghold’s gates were sealed, denying passage amid the turmoil.

Now known as the under ruins, the area is infested with beasts and undead sealife, preying on any unfortunate wanderers who dare to tread its shattered corridors.

The island's volcano, devoid of any recorded volcanic activity, holds immense significance in Old Folk history. Within its depths rests Faidon's most prized possession, meticulously safeguarded and strongly secured by Faidon himself.

The Western Ruins bear witness to the Old Folk's legacy, their once-great architecture now weathered by time and war. Carvings on the walls narrate tales of heroes and struggles, serving as a silent testament to the civilization's past.

In this strange place, I'm surrounded by bizarre creatures and a pervasive sense of hopelessness. The temple smells awful, and despite reading all the stone tablets, most of the information doesn't make sense.

The word "Leviathan" keeps popping up everywhere, suggesting its importance. But what is its significance? And who are these mark keepers I keep reading about? I need clear and straightforward answers.

Skeletons, animated and aggressive, haunt my every step. Their relentless attacks leave an indelible mark on my psyche. The horror of this place seems endless.

Despite the despair that threatens to consume me, I can't help but notice the stark contrast between myself and these wretched creatures. They were human once, like me. It's a grim reminder of the fate that could befall anyone in this forsaken land.

I try not to dwell on my despair. There's still a lot to explore and many creatures to encounter. I just hope some of them are friendly. As for my crew, I can't shake the worry about what happened to them amidst all this chaos. Where could they be?

Even amidst the destruction, this garden remains oddly soothing... but there's no time to dwell on it. I'm too busy fighting these beasts to fully appreciate the scene.

I've become more skilled at fighting these fish-men, but I can't shake the thought of what drove them to this state. How did this island turn into such a nightmare?

Recently, I encountered two creatures named Yonis and Calanthus. Despite sharing the appearance of the hostile fish-men, they displayed kindness and lacked the bloodlust of their kin. It's perplexing, and I wonder what keeps them sane amidst this madness. They believe I'm here to change the island's fate, to save them all. That's nonsense, of course. How would such a responsibility ever fall upon me?

Nevertheless, I must decide my next move.

Who would have thought there'd be friendly fish-men, or rather, OldFolk? Yonis gets a bit uncomfortable when I refer to him as a fish. I'll stick with OldFolk then.

Despite the suffocating weight of our situation, Calanthus and Yonis seem to place their faith in me. It's a heavy burden, but being a symbol of hope for them brings some sense of purpose.

In moments like these, it's easy to forget our impending doom. Making friends like Calanthus and Yonis makes me question why I was so fixated on finding my own crew. Whatever happened here is bigger than all of us.

Since arriving on this cursed island, I've encountered a mix of creatures, some hostile, others guiding me toward strength. But now, lying amidst these ruins, I realize I might be about to fail in my promise.

Before me stands the epitome of my nightmares: the Giant King Crab. Escaping its clutches and continuing my quest to free us from this land is essential. However, this beast poses a challenge unlike any I've faced.

Yonis and Calanthus, who once looked to me as a beacon of hope, would be disappointed if they knew I might not make it. But I can't give up. I must summon all my strength to overcome this trial and continue our journey to freedom.

As I delve deeper into this accursed territory, I find myself pondering an escape route. As a member of the Imperial Navy, perseverance is ingrained in me. Courage is our creed, driving us ever forward, but these maxims seem woefully inadequate in the face of such malevolence. The corruption here feels palpable, gnawing at the edges of my sanity. Will there ever be respite from this torment?

All that remains is to salvage what good we can from this chaos. Perhaps uncovering relics amidst this nightmare could redeem our suffering. Yet, I must determine which among our crew has the fortitude to join me in this pursuit.

Gathering a group of my men, I've organized an expedition under the guise of further exploration and the slim possibility of finding an escape route. Yet, deep down, I harbor doubts about the existence of such an exit. Regardless, I cling to the hope that our journey will yield something valuable.

With each passing moment on this cursed terrain, my mind becomes increasingly clouded. Uncertainty shrouds our expedition, and I find myself questioning the outcome. Despite the looming dangers, it's becoming evident that my own well-being should take precedence during this ominous journey.

Here we are, right through the mountains, with my crew slumbering, unaware of the treasures that surround us. The glint of gold and the allure of relics beckon to me, yet my comrades remain oblivious. I must seize this opportunity to claim the riches for myself, even if it means resorting to drastic measures.

Stranded on this cursed island, survival has become a solitary pursuit. If I am ever to escape this wretched place, I must prioritize my own interests. I vow to leave no stone unturned in my quest for wealth and fortune, for when the chance of liberation presents itself, I will emerge with my pockets laden with treasure.

The weight of regret presses heavily upon me, yet in the face of the riches I've obtained, I cannot help but justify my actions. As I returned with the coveted gold in hand, a comrade stirred and caught sight of the relic. I knew I had to act swiftly to prevent them from alerting the others, for I couldn't bear the thought of sharing the treasure with anyone else.

Back at camp, I must maintain a facade of innocence, ensuring no one suspects the truth of what transpired in the cavern. It's all too easy to attribute the tragedy to the monstrous inhabitants of this cursed land.

With the blood of my own comrades staining my hands, my singular focus now lies in safeguarding these relics and escaping this accursed place at any cost.

Before settling our camp at the High Peaks, I thoroughly inspected the surrounding area to ensure it was suitable for myself and the navy men. Not far away, I stumbled upon an unusual scene where a large crew of pirates was engaged in something quite odd.

 I could only watch as the captain barked orders to his men, instructing them to manipulate the switches in various ways, trying to get some sequence right. Watching them fail repeatedly, and seeing their deaths one after another, I made sure to jot down every combination they tried. It became clear to me that there was only one pattern left for them to attempt.

 <Light> I noted down the sequence: standing in front of the central snake-like statue, facing the other side of the room, activate the middle switch on the right, followed by the furthest left switch from the statue, then the closest switch on the same row, and subsequently the switch directly in front of it. Finally, the last switch on the right row should be toggled, followed by the middle left switch.</>

 Naturally, I was tempted to give the sequence a shot myself. But seeing the last crew member meet his end and the subsequent transformation of their captain into a wild beast shook me to the core. There's something seriously off about this place.

 Nevertheless, I made sure to note down the sequence for future reference. Despite the dangers, I can't help but wonder what happens if someone actually cracks that puzzle. I guess there’s only one way to find out.

Under the Abyssal Corruption, once peaceful island clams turned hostile, gaining new abilities that endanger inhabitants. Some can shoot fire, others bite, and some even float, united by a newfound bloodthirst.

As a result, all the crabs on the island became hostile, with some exhibiting newfound abilities previously unseen in their species.

The Abyssal Corruption brought several changes to the island's underwater creatures. Jellyfish Big Mama epitomizes the malevolent traits of the other abyssal jellyfish that infest the island, serving as a haunting reminder of the Abyssal Corruption's darkest manifestations. The King Crab stands as a grim testament to the most sinister effects of Abyssal Corruption. Transformed into a monstrous beast, it possesses enhanced size and deadly abilities. Additionally, it wields the power to summon other abyssal crabs, using them to dominate its prey.

Under the influence of the Abyssal Corruption, the fungi on the island underwent a huge transformation. Harmless mushrooms gained lethal abilities, becoming capable of releasing poison, attacking trespassers, and chasing away anyone who ventures too close to them.
